author: Marcus R. Brown
description:
Unblocks the `typedoc` `0.28.19` → `0.28.20` upgrade that #1812 has been stuck on.

## The failure

```
[error] The plugin typedoc-plugin-frontmatter could not be loaded
[error] Cannot find package '<root>/node_modules/typedoc/index.js'
        imported from .../typedoc-plugin-frontmatter/dist/comments.js
        Did you mean to import "typedoc/dist/index.js"?
[error] Unknown option 'frontmatterGlobals'
```

CI-only. It never reproduced locally, under an identical lockfile, pnpm 11.25.0, and `shamefullyHoist: true`.

## What it actually was

`typedoc-plugin-frontmatter@1.3.1` imports `typedoc` with a bare specifier but declares no dependency on it — not in `dependencies`, not in `peerDependencies`, which list only `{"typedoc-plugin-markdown": ">=4.9.0"}`. pnpm therefore never links `typedoc` into the plugin's own `node_modules`, and resolution walks up to whatever hoisting leaves at the workspace root.

That is where the two environments diverged. Probing the runner directly:

```
node_modules/typedoc/          ← NOT a symlink
node_modules/typedoc/dist
node_modules/typedoc/dist/types    ← the entire contents
```

No `package.json`. Node cannot read an `exports` map that is not there, so it falls back to a legacy directory-index lookup and asks for `node_modules/typedoc/index.js`, which does not exist. Hence the error, and hence Node's "did you mean `typedoc/dist/index.js`?" hint — it never got as far as `exports`.

Locally the same hoist produces a complete symlink into `.pnpm`, `exports` resolves normally, and everything works. The plugin's own `node_modules` has sibling links for `typedoc-plugin-markdown` and `yaml`, but none for `typedoc`, on both platforms — the difference is entirely in what the root fallback happens to contain.
